The engineering value of this path is that it transforms the unanswerable question "Is AI reliable?" into a measurable question: "To what extent is AI reliable?" — each promotion means that AI's performance under human supervision has been fully observed. bnqa25:353: The deepest insight of the five-layer cost methodology is the one-way dependency between layers: the bottom layer (usage habits) has the highest returns but the lowest ceiling, while the top layer (Agent architecture) requires the largest upfront investment but delivers sustained marginal returns. A common mistake is skipping the bottom layers and going straight to architectural changes — if a single session mixes multiple tasks and never compacts, context bloat will multiply and consume the gains from upper-layer architecture optimization. Therefore, "usage habits → model routing → context engineering → code graph → Agent architecture" is both the implementation order and the ROI ranking: each upper layer solves structural waste that the layer below cannot reach. Subagent isolation deserves particular caution — it appears to "offload the burden to subagents," but in reality it is independently billed context. Only when combined with Orchestrator-Worker responsibility splitting (the main agent only plans and adjudicates; subagents prioritize reading git diff and key snippets rather than full files) can total token consumption be truly reduced.
